title: David and Goliath
subtitle: A young shepherd defeats an invincible giant

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: In a valley between two mountains, two armies stood face to face: the Israelites and the Philistines. Everyone trembled with fear.

steps.speaker: Goliath
steps.text: Do you have the courage to face a giant? Send your best warrior! But I doubt anyone is as strong as I am.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Goliath was nearly three meters tall. No one dared to approach him. For forty days the giant had been challenging the army of Israel.
Why were the Israelites afraid of Goliath?
options: Because he was very large and strong
Because he was the king's friend
Because he had magic weapons
steps.answer: Because he was very large and strong

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: David was a young shepherd who took care of his father's sheep. When his father sent him to bring food to his brothers in war, David saw Goliath.

steps.speaker: David
steps.text: Why are you afraid? I will fight this giant! The Lord will help me, for he is with me.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: You are too young! Goliath is a trained warrior. He will crush you like an insect!

steps.speaker: David
steps.text: The Lord delivered me from the paws of the lion and the bear when I was a shepherd. He will also save me from Goliath.
What previous experience was David talking about?
options: Fights he faced while protecting his sheep
Battles he participated in in Saul's kingdom
Special training for war
steps.answer: Fights he faced while protecting his sheep

steps.speaker: King Saul
steps.text: Can you fight Goliath? Use my armor and my sword. Thus you will be protected.

steps.speaker: David
steps.text: Thank you, but I cannot fight with this armor. I'm not used to it. I prefer to trust in the Lord.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: David took his sling and five smooth stones from the river. Then he walked confidently toward Goliath.

steps.speaker: Goliath
steps.text: You come to defeat me with a sling? What a foolish boy! I will make you return!

steps.speaker: David
steps.text: You come against me with sword and spear. But I come in the name of the Lord of Hosts!
What did David trust in to defeat Goliath?
options: In the Lord and his faith
In the strength of his own arm
In the help of the soldiers
steps.answer: In the Lord and his faith

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: David put a stone in his sling and threw it with force. The stone flew through the air and struck Goliath's forehead.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The giant fell like a pine tree in a storm. Goliath never rose again. All the nation of Israel saw God's miracle.

steps.speaker: People
steps.text: David! David! He defeated Goliath! The Lord is with him!
What was the main lesson of this story?
options: Faith in God is more powerful than any giant
You don't need armor to fight
Children are better warriors than adults
steps.answer: Faith in God is more powerful than any giant

title: Daniel in the Lion's Den
subtitle: A man of faith faces death with courage

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Daniel was a wise young man in the kingdom of Babylon. King Nebuchadnezzar loved him and made him one of the most powerful princes.

steps.speaker: Jealous Princes
steps.text: Daniel has too much power! We need to find a reason to accuse him to the king and remove him from his position.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The princes looked for flaws in Daniel's character. But he was honorable and faithful. Every day, Daniel prayed to God.
Why did the princes want to defeat Daniel?
options: Because they were jealous of his power and wisdom
Because Daniel stole gold from the kingdom
Because Daniel was a foreigner
steps.answer: Because they were jealous of his power and wisdom

steps.speaker: Jealous Princes
steps.text: We know how to defeat Daniel! Let's ask the king to make a decree. No one can pray to anyone except the king for thirty days!

steps.speaker: King Darius
steps.text: Very well. Anyone who prays will be cast into the lion's den.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Daniel heard about the decree. But he did not stop praying to God. He continued praying three times a day, as he had always done.

steps.speaker: Daniel
steps.text: My God is more important than my life. I will not stop praying to Him, no matter what the cost.
How did Daniel respond to the king's decree?
options: He continued praying to God faithfully
He stopped praying to save his life
He prayed only in secret at night
steps.answer: He continued praying to God faithfully

steps.speaker: Jealous Princes
steps.text: King! Daniel disobeys your decree! He prayed to his God three times today! According to your law, he must be cast into the lion's den!

steps.speaker: King Darius
steps.text: No! Daniel is a just and wise man. But my own law compels me. May the God of Daniel save you!

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Daniel was taken to the lion's den. A great stone was placed over the opening. The king sealed the den with his ring to ensure that no one would save him.

steps.speaker: King Darius
steps.text: Daniel, may your God protect you. I spent the whole night praying for you.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The king awoke before dawn, troubled. He ran quickly to the lion's den. There, he called out for Daniel.
What did the king do when he woke up?
options: He ran to the den to see if Daniel was alive
He slept until late
He ate his breakfast normally
steps.answer: He ran to the den to see if Daniel was alive

steps.speaker: King Darius
steps.text: Daniel! Are you alive? Could your God save you?

steps.speaker: Daniel
steps.text: My king! My God sent an angel and closed the mouths of the lions. They did not harm me because I am innocent before God and the king.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Daniel was brought back alive! Not even a thread of his clothing was damaged. The lions respected him and protected him!

steps.speaker: King Darius
steps.text: Let all kingdoms know! The God of Daniel is the living and true God. He saves those who believe in Him!
What miracle did God perform for Daniel?
options: He sent an angel and closed the mouths of the lions
The lions became vegetarians
Daniel flew out of the den
steps.answer: He sent an angel and closed the mouths of the lions

title: Esther Before the King
subtitle: A queen's courage saves her people

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Esther was a very beautiful and wise young Jewish woman. She became queen of the Persian Empire, but kept her Jewish identity secret.

steps.speaker: Mordecai
steps.text: Esther, I need to tell you something terrible. An evil man named Haman convinced the king to order the death of all Jews in the kingdom!

steps.speaker: Esther
steps.text: This is horrible! My people will be destroyed! What can I do?

steps.speaker: Mordecai
steps.text: Perhaps God put you on the throne for just this moment. You are the only one who can speak to the king and ask for your people's lives.
Why did Mordecai believe Esther could save her people?
options: Because she was queen and had access to the king
Because she was very beautiful
Because she was the king's daughter
steps.answer: Because she was queen and had access to the king

steps.speaker: Esther
steps.text: But there is a problem. No one can approach the king without being invited. If he does not extend his golden scepter, I can be condemned to death!

steps.speaker: Mordecai
steps.text: Esther, you must be courageous. First, ask all the Jews to fast and pray. Then go before the king.

steps.speaker: Esther
steps.text: Yes, I will do this. Even if I die, I will die trying to save my people.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Esther gathered her strength and prepared for a special meal with the king. She wore her finest clothes and presented herself before him.
How did Esther prepare to speak to the king?
options: She asked people to pray for her and prepared herself with grace
She shouted and demanded her right
She tried to deceive the king with lies
steps.answer: She asked people to pray for her and prepared herself with grace

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: My Queen Esther! Welcome! What do you wish? I can grant you even half of my kingdom!

steps.speaker: Esther
steps.text: My king, I ask that you and Haman come to a banquet that I have prepared especially.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Esther invited the king and Haman to a banquet. That night, she gathered courage to reveal the truth.

steps.speaker: Esther
steps.text: My king! I ask for my life and the life of my people! Someone wants to destroy us! It is Haman, that evil man!

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: What? Haman wants to destroy you? Esther, you are my queen! No one will harm you while I live!
How did the king respond when he learned of Haman's plan?
options: He was against Haman and defended Queen Esther
He said Esther was lying
He apologized to Haman
steps.answer: He was against Haman and defended Queen Esther

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The king issued a new decree. All the Jews were saved from Haman's plan. Esther became a heroine, and her courage saved her people.

steps.speaker: Jewish People
steps.text: Hallelujah! Esther is our queen! She was courageous and saved us! Praise be to the Lord!

title: Jonah and the Great Fish
subtitle: A prophet learns about obedience and compassion

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: God spoke to Jonah: 'Go to the city of Nineveh and warn the people that if they do not repent of their sins, the city will be destroyed.'

steps.speaker: Jonah
steps.text: I will not! Nineveh is an enemy of my people. Let God destroy them! I will flee in this boat.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Jonah fled from God, but the Lord is faster. A great storm began to stir the sea.

steps.speaker: Sailor 1
steps.text: What is happening? I have sailed for forty years and never seen a storm so horrible!
Why did the storm begin?
options: Because God sent it to bring Jonah back
Because there was a natural hurricane in that region
Because the sailors did something wrong
steps.answer: Because God sent it to bring Jonah back

steps.speaker: Sailor 2
steps.text: Is there someone here who fled from his God? The storm is punishing someone!
Yes, it was me. I fled from my God. Take me and throw me into the sea. Then the storm will stop.
steps.speaker: Jonah

steps.text: Are you sure? You don't want to live?
steps.speaker: Sailor 1
Jonah
steps.text: God is more important than my life. Let me pay for my sin.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The sailors, sadly, threw Jonah into the turbulent sea. But God prepared a great fish to swallow him.
What happened to Jonah when he was thrown into the sea?
options: A great fish swallowed him, but he did not die
He drowned immediately
A great bird saved him
steps.answer: A great fish swallowed him, but he did not die

steps.speaker: Jonah
steps.text: I am in the belly of a huge fish! It is so dark here. But God is still with me. I will pray and repent.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights. In that dark time, he learned an important lesson.

steps.speaker: Jonah
steps.text: God, I was wrong! You are merciful. I will go to Nineveh and do what you asked. I will preach your repentance.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: God heard Jonah's prayer. The great fish spat him back onto dry land. Jonah was alive!
What did Jonah learn during his experience?
options: That God is merciful and deserves obedience
That he should never obey God
That the sea is dangerous
steps.answer: That God is merciful and deserves obedience

steps.speaker: Jonah
steps.text: Now I will go to Nineveh as God asked. I still don't like them, but I must warn them that they must repent.

steps.speaker: People of Nineveh
steps.text: Listen! Jonah says our city will be destroyed if we don't repent! Let's all repent and ask the God of Jonah to forgive us!

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: All the people of Nineveh heard and repented. God had compassion on them and forgave the city. God's will was fulfilled.

title: Ruth and Naomi
subtitle: Loyalty and compassion in a woman's heart

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Naomi was a widow Israelite woman, and her daughter-in-law Ruth was a foreigner. Both had lost everything and were desperate.

steps.speaker: Naomi
steps.text: Ruth, dear, you should return to your land. I have nothing to offer you here. Your life can be better with your own people.

steps.speaker: Ruth
steps.text: Naomi, I will go with you! Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God. I will not leave you alone.
Why did Ruth want to stay with Naomi?
options: Because she loved Naomi and was loyal
Because she wanted to earn money
Because she was afraid to return
steps.answer: Because she loved Naomi and was loyal

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Ruth and Naomi arrived in Bethlehem at harvest time. Ruth went to the fields and asked permission to glean the grain left behind by the harvesters.

steps.speaker: Ruth
steps.text: Please, may I glean in your field? I promise to work hard to get food for my mother-in-law.

steps.speaker: Boaz
steps.text: Of course you can, dear girl. I have heard about your loyalty to Naomi. That is worthy of praise.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Boaz was a rich and respected man. He saw Ruth's loyalty and began to love her. He protected her in the fields.
How did Boaz treat Ruth in the fields?
options: With kindness, offering water and protection
With coldness and contempt
He ignored her completely
steps.answer: With kindness, offering water and protection

steps.speaker: Boaz
steps.text: Ruth, I want to ask you to marry me. You are a woman worthy of honor and loyalty. I would like to care for you and Naomi.

steps.speaker: Ruth
steps.text: Yes! You are so kind to me. I accept being your wife.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Ruth and Boaz married. They had a son named Obed, who became the grandfather of King David.

steps.speaker: Naomi
steps.text: Praise be to God! My daughter-in-law redeemed me and gave me joy. Now we have hope and a future!
What was the result of Ruth's loyalty?
options: She found love, security, and a place in God's history
She remained poor forever
Naomi became unhappy again
steps.answer: She found love, security, and a place in God's history

title: The Birth of Jesus
subtitle: God enters the world as a baby

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Mary was a young woman from Nazareth. One day, the angel Gabriel appeared to her with surprising news.

steps.speaker: Gabriel
steps.text: Do not be afraid, Mary! You have been chosen among all women. You will conceive and bear a son called Jesus.

steps.speaker: Mary
steps.text: How can this be? I have no husband. How can I have a son?

steps.speaker: Gabriel
steps.text: The Holy Spirit will come upon you. The son will be called the Son of God. His kingdom will have no end.
How did Mary respond to the angel's news?
options: With faith, saying she would do God's will
With anger and disbelief
Fleeing from the angel in fear
steps.answer: With faith, saying she would do God's will

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Mary was betrothed to Joseph, a righteous carpenter. When he learned of Mary, he planned to leave her secretly. But an angel appeared to him in a dream.

steps.speaker: Angel
steps.text: Joseph, do not be afraid. The son of Mary is of the Holy Spirit. Call him Jesus, for he will save his people from sin.

steps.speaker: Joseph
steps.text: I understand now. I will accept this mission. I will be the earthly father of Jesus and care for Mary.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem because the emperor ordered a census. Everyone needed to register in their hometown.
Why did Mary and Joseph go to Bethlehem?
options: Because of the census ordered by the emperor
Because they wanted a trip
Because their relative lived there
steps.answer: Because of the census ordered by the emperor

steps.speaker: Mary
steps.text: I need to find a place to give birth. My son is arriving!

steps.speaker: Innkeeper
steps.text: I'm sorry, but there are no rooms. The inn is full. You can stay in the stable if you like.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Jesus was born in a simple stable. Mary wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a manger full of straw.

steps.speaker: Shepherds
steps.text: What is this brightness? What is happening in the sky?

steps.speaker: Angel
steps.text: Do not fear! I have good news of great joy for all people. Today in the city of David, the Savior has been born!
Who were the first to know about the birth of Jesus?
options: The shepherds in the fields, when the angel appeared to them
The wise men
The Roman emperor
steps.answer: The shepherds in the fields, when the angel appeared to them

steps.speaker: Shepherds
steps.text: Let's go to Bethlehem and see the baby! The angel said he is wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger!

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The shepherds ran and found Jesus, Mary, and Joseph. They worshipped the baby and told everyone what they heard.

steps.speaker: Wise Men from the East
steps.text: A new star has appeared! It means a great king has been born. Let's go and worship him with gifts.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The wise men traveled from far away following a star. They found Jesus and offered him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

title: Jesus Calms the Storm
subtitle: Jesus has power even over the elements of nature

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Jesus and his disciples were in a boat on the Sea of Galilee. Jesus was so tired he fell asleep.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Suddenly, a terrible storm began. The wind blew fiercely and huge waves beat against the boat.

steps.speaker: Disciple 1
steps.text: Sirs! We are sinking! The boat is filling with water! We are going to die!

steps.speaker: Disciple 2
steps.text: Where is Jesus? Why doesn't he help us? Doesn't he care?
Why were the disciples afraid?
options: Because a violent storm surrounded them
Because they couldn't swim
Because they heard about pirates
steps.answer: Because a violent storm surrounded them

steps.speaker: Disciple 1
steps.text: Jesus! Wake up! Please, wake up! We are dying!
Jesus woke up and saw fear on his disciples' faces. He got up with calm and authority.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Jesus
steps.text: Why are you afraid? Where is your faith?

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Peace! Be still!
Jesus spoke to the wind and the waves. And immediately, a great peace came down. The wind ceased and the waters calmed.
steps.speaker: Narrator

steps.text: How did the storm end?
options: Jesus ordered the wind and waves to calm down
The disciples rowed away from the storm
Another ship helped them
steps.answer: Jesus ordered the wind and waves to calm down

steps.speaker: Disciple 2
steps.text: Jesus! What kind of man are you? Even the wind and sea obey you!

steps.speaker: Disciple 3
steps.text: He must be the Messiah! No one else has this power!

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: You saw my power. Know that I have authority even over nature. Trust me, for I am always with you.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: All the disciples were filled with amazement. They understood that Jesus was not just a teacher, but the Son of God.

title: Zacchaeus
subtitle: A small man finds salvation in Jesus

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Zacchaeus was a tax collector in Jericho. He was very small in stature and very rich, but hated by everyone.
Zacchaeus is a traitor! He collects more taxes than he should and keeps the money. He is a snake!
steps.speaker: People of Jericho
Narrator
steps.text: One day, Jesus passed through Jericho. Crowds followed him. Zacchaeus wanted to see Jesus, but he was too short.

steps.speaker: Zacchaeus
steps.text: I can't see! This crowd is too big. No one will let a tax collector pass in front.
Why did Zacchaeus have difficulty seeing Jesus?
options: Because he was very short and the crowd was large
Because his eyes were closed
Because he was very far away
steps.answer: Because he was very short and the crowd was large

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Zacchaeus saw an opportunity. He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus pass.

steps.speaker: Zacchaeus
steps.text: Perfect! From up in this tree I can see Jesus without any problem!
When Jesus passed near the tree, he looked up and saw Zacchaeus.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Jesus
steps.text: Zacchaeus! Come down! I want to go to your house today!

steps.speaker: Zacchaeus
steps.text: You want to come to my house? I am so hated! But I'll come down quick!
How did Zacchaeus feel when Jesus noticed him?
options: Surprised and happy because Jesus chose him
Furious because Jesus saw him
Indifferent
steps.answer: Surprised and happy because Jesus chose him

steps.speaker: People of Jericho
steps.text: How terrible! Jesus is going to the house of Zacchaeus? A corrupt tax collector?
As they ate, Zacchaeus was transformed by his encounter with Jesus. He saw his sin and wanted to change.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Zacchaeus
steps.text: Jesus, I want to change! I will give half of my possessions to the poor and give back four times what I stole!

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Today salvation has entered your house. You are truly a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.
How was Zacchaeus transformed?
options: He repented and changed his life, wanting to make amends
He continued stealing as before
He tried to buy Jesus' favor
steps.answer: He repented and changed his life, wanting to make amends

title: The Samaritan Woman
subtitle: Jesus offers living water to an abandoned woman

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Jesus was traveling from Judea to Galilee and had to pass through Samaria. It was hot noon.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Jesus sat by a well. A Samaritan woman came alone to draw water.

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Please, give me some water to drink.

steps.speaker: Samaritan Woman
steps.text: How is it that you, being a Jew, ask water from me, a Samaritan woman? Jews don't have dealings with us.
Why was the woman surprised by Jesus' request?
options: Because Jews generally avoided Samaritans
Because she was afraid of water
Because it was night and there shouldn't be men
steps.answer: Because Jews generally avoided Samaritans

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: If you knew who I am, you would ask me for water. I would give you living water that would never run dry.

steps.speaker: Samaritan Woman
steps.text: Living water? Sir, you don't even have a bucket and the well is deep. How can you draw living water?

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Anyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again. But whoever drinks the water I give will never be thirsty again.

steps.speaker: Samaritan Woman
steps.text: Sir, give me this water so I will not be thirsty or have to come here to draw water!
What did the woman ask of Jesus?
options: The living water that Jesus offered
More gold and silver
That he come back another day
steps.answer: The living water that Jesus offered

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Go call your husband and come back.

steps.speaker: Samaritan Woman
steps.text: I have no husband.

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: You are right. You have had five husbands and the one you now have is not your husband. You have spoken the truth.
The woman realized that Jesus knew her entire story. She had been hurt and rejected many times. But Jesus did not judge her.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Samaritan Woman
steps.text: Sir, you are a prophet! Now I understand that you are the Messiah we have been waiting for!

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: I am he. True worship is not on mountains or in temples, but in spirit and in truth.
How was the woman transformed?
options: She recognized Jesus as the Messiah and testified to others
She continued with the same empty life
She tried to deceive Jesus
steps.answer: She recognized Jesus as the Messiah and testified to others

steps.speaker: Samaritan Woman
steps.text: People of my city! Come! I found the Messiah! He knows me! See what he did for me!
Many Samaritans believed in Jesus through that woman's testimony. Her life was transformed by the love of Jesus.
steps.speaker: Narrator

title: The Prodigal Son
subtitle: The love of a father who never abandons

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: A certain man had two sons. One day, the younger son said to his father: 'Father, give me my inheritance now!'

steps.speaker: Father
steps.text: My son, you want your inheritance already? Very well. I will divide my property.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The younger son took his inheritance and went far away. He lived wildly, spending everything on parties and pleasures.
How did the younger son use his inheritance?
options: He spent it all on parties and pleasures
He invested in business
He saved and invested carefully
steps.answer: He spent it all on parties and pleasures

steps.speaker: Younger Son
steps.text: Finally I'm free! No one can tell me what to do! I will enjoy life!
But when the money ran out, a great famine came to the land. The son had nothing.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Younger Son
steps.text: I'm dying of hunger! I need a job! What can I do?

steps.speaker: Employer
steps.text: You can work taking care of my pigs. You will feed the pigs.
The fallen son began to feed the pigs. He was so hungry that he would have eaten what the pigs ate.
steps.speaker: Narrator

steps.text: What was the son's situation when the money ran out?
options: He was without anything, working with pigs, hungry
He found a well-paid job
His father found him and took him back
steps.answer: He was without anything, working with pigs, hungry

steps.speaker: Younger Son
steps.text: What a fool I was! My father has many servants and they all have enough food. But I'm here dying of hunger.

steps.speaker: Younger Son
steps.text: I will go back to my father. I will say: Father, I have sinned against you. I am not worthy to be your son. Let me be one of your servants.
The son got up and began the long journey back. He was repentant and humiliated.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Narrator
steps.text: But when still far away, his father saw him. The father's heart overflowed with love and compassion.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.text: My son! My son has come back! The one I thought was lost is now found!

steps.speaker: Father
steps.text: Quick! Bring the best clothes! Prepare a great feast! My son is back!
How did the father respond when he saw his son return?
options: With love and forgiveness, offering a feast
With anger and punishment
With indifference
steps.answer: With love and forgiveness, offering a feast

steps.speaker: Younger Son
steps.text: Father! I have sinned against you! I am not worthy to be your son...

steps.speaker: Father
steps.text: Hush, my son! You have come back! That is all that matters! You were lost and now you are found!

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The father embraced his son and kissed him. All the joy of the home was restored. God loves us in the same way.

title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
subtitle: Jesus has power even over death

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Lazarus was a friend of Jesus. He lived in Bethany with his sisters Mary and Martha. One day, Lazarus became very ill.

steps.speaker: Mary
steps.text: Martha, Lazarus is getting worse! We must send word to Jesus! He can heal him!

steps.speaker: Martha
steps.text: Yes! Let's send someone right away! Jesus loves him. When he hears that Lazarus is sick, he will come running!
Why did Mary and Martha want Jesus to know Lazarus was sick?
options: Because they trusted that Jesus could heal him
Because they wanted Jesus to suffer
Because they had no money for doctors
steps.answer: Because they trusted that Jesus could heal him

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The sisters sent a message, but Jesus did not go immediately. He waited two days before traveling.
When Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been dead for four days. Martha came out to meet him.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Martha
steps.text: Lord! If you had come when Lazarus was sick, he would not have died! But even now, I know God listens to you always!

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Your brother will rise again.

steps.speaker: Martha
steps.text: I know he will rise again in the resurrection, on the last day.

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live. Do you believe this?
What did Jesus promise about himself?
options: That He is the resurrection and the life
That no one would die
That He would reign for a thousand years
steps.answer: That He is the resurrection and the life

steps.speaker: Martha
steps.text: Yes, Lord! I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God!
Jesus asked them to take him to Lazarus' tomb. The stone was rolled away.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Jesus
steps.text: Father, I thank you for hearing me. Father, raise Lazarus!
Lazarus came out of the tomb! His arms and legs were bound with wrappings and his face was covered with a cloth.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Jesus
steps.text: Loose him and let him go! He is alive!

steps.speaker: Mary and Martha
steps.text: Lazarus! You came back! Jesus gave our brother back to us!
How did Jesus raise Lazarus?
options: By prayer and God's power
Through medical techniques
By magic
steps.answer: By prayer and God's power

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: All who saw the miracle believed in Jesus. Death could not hold back before God's power.

title: The Road to Emmaus
subtitle: We recognize Jesus when he reveals himself

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: After Jesus' crucifixion, two disciples were walking on the road to Emmaus. They were sad and confused.

steps.speaker: Disciple 1
steps.text: We had hope that Jesus was the Messiah. But he was crucified. Now everything is lost.

steps.speaker: Disciple 2
steps.text: Yes. And women said his tomb is empty. How can this be? Where will salvation come from now?

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: As they talked, a man approached and began to walk with them. It was the risen Jesus, but their eyes were veiled.

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: What do you discuss as you walk? You seem sad.
Are you a stranger? Don't you know what happened in Jerusalem?
steps.speaker: Disciple 1

steps.text: Why didn't the disciples recognize Jesus?
options: Because their eyes were veiled by God
Because Jesus had changed clothes
Because it was too dark
steps.answer: Because their eyes were veiled by God

steps.speaker: Disciple 2
steps.text: Tell us what happened. A man named Jesus of Nazareth was mighty in deeds. But the leaders crucified him.

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: O foolish ones! Slow of heart to believe! Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer and enter his glory?

steps.speaker: Jesus
steps.text: Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things about himself.
As they walked, Jesus opened their minds to understand the Scriptures. Their hearts burned with hope.
steps.speaker: Narrator

steps.text: How did Jesus help the disciples understand?
options: By explaining the Scriptures about the Messiah
By telling stories about travels
By asking to borrow money
steps.answer: By explaining the Scriptures about the Messiah

steps.speaker: Disciple 1
steps.text: O stranger, the night is falling. Come and stay with us. Don't abandon us!
Jesus entered to stay with them. When they sat at the table, Jesus took the bread, blessed it, and gave it to them.
steps.speaker: Narrator

steps.text: At that moment, the eyes of the disciples were opened and they recognized Jesus. But he disappeared from their sight.
steps.speaker: Narrator
Disciple 2
steps.text: It was Jesus! Didn't our hearts burn when he spoke to us on the way and opened the Scriptures?

steps.speaker: Disciple 1
steps.text: Let's go back to Jerusalem! We must tell the others that Jesus has risen!
How did the disciples recognize Jesus?
options: When he broke bread at the table
When they heard his voice
When they saw him risen
steps.answer: When he broke bread at the table

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The disciples returned to Jerusalem with joy. They found the other disciples and shared that Jesus had risen and revealed himself to them.
